LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: SEQUENCING IDEAS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Spelling (2 sessions) • Correct spelling of words • 
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas, part of Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Spelling (2 sessions) • Correct spelling of words •  in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you form a paragraph?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify features of a well-developed paragraph,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. organise a short imaginative paragraph for logical sequence,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify features of a well-developed paragraph,

   Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. organise a short imaginative paragraph for logical sequence,

   Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

   Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to research on the features of a well written paragraph e.g. neat and legible, well sequenced, well paragraphed, correct spelling,

2. reorganise jumbled up words to form meaningful sentences,

3. team up to compete in rearranging jumbled up sentences to form a coherent paragraph on sports and games,

4. present their well sequenced paragraphs to the class for review.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to research on the features of a well written paragraph e.g. neat and legible, well sequenced, well paragraphed, correct spelling,
2. reorganise jumbled up words to form meaningful sentences,
3. team up to compete in rearranging jumbled up sentences to form a coherent paragraph on sports and games,
4. present their well sequenced paragraphs to the class for review.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner follows simple instructions to reorganise jumbled up

words to form meaningful sentences.

• Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making when collaborating

with peers to research on the features of a well written paragraph.

Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits accountability to accept input when presenting their well sequenced

paragraphs to the class for review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health and fitness: This is enhanced as the learner talks about sports and games of their preference with their peers.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept about sports and games to their learning in Creative Arts.
